title: 领导力 Day 77：scope 变大之后：放大自己，带资深的人，带 manager
title_en: Leadership Day 77: Leading at a Bigger Scope

questions.question: scope 变大后你不再待在细节里。要及早发现哪条工作流快出事，文章推荐看什么？
options: 每条工作流再配一位副负责人，双人负责更保险
所有设计评审都抄送给你，由你亲自逐份把关
盯紧各条工作流每周的红黄绿状态，一旦变红就立即亲自下场介入
每周各 DRI 给下个里程碑打的信心分趋势，下滑就去问
questions.explanation: 真正有用的信号在趋势里，等到变红已经晚了；从绿直接跳红还应当作报告失真处理。一条工作流配两个负责人，等于没人负责；审每一份设计会让你成为瓶颈。
questions.question_en: With a bigger scope you're no longer in the details. To spot early which workstream is heading for trouble, what does the piece recommend watching?
options_en: Adding a co-owner to each workstream so two people share responsibility
Having every design review copied to you so you can vet each one yourself
Each workstream's red/yellow/green status, stepping in personally once it turns red
The trend in each DRI's weekly confidence score for the next milestone; ask when it drops
questions.explanation_en: The useful signal is in the trend; by the time it's red it's too late, and a jump straight from green to red should be treated as a reporting failure. Two owners means no owner, and reviewing every design makes you the bottleneck.

questions.question: 一位同级的资深工程师不同意你的技术方向，而这件事事后很容易回滚。按文章的做法，怎么处理？
options: 立刻一起去找上级裁决，避免在分歧上拖延时间
你负责优先级、取舍和承诺，所以由你拍板，他保留意见全力执行
先把争议冻结，等收集到更多数据之后再一起决定
先复述他的观点直到他认可，再让他按自己的方式试一个周期
questions.explanation: 分歧先复述对方观点；容易回滚的，让他按他的方式试一个周期并约好检查点；难回滚的才摊开谈、必要时一起找上级。对同级的人拿职位压人，这张牌每用一次就弱一分。
questions.question_en: A senior engineer at your level disagrees with your technical direction, and the decision is easy to reverse later. Per the piece, how should you handle it?
options_en: Escalate to your manager together right away to avoid dragging it out
You own trade-offs and commitments, so you decide and they disagree and commit
Freeze the dispute until more data comes in, then decide together
Restate their view until they agree you've got it, then let them try their way for a cycle
questions.explanation_en: First restate their view; if it's easy to reverse, let them try it for a cycle with an agreed checkpoint; only hard-to-reverse calls get hashed out openly and, if needed, escalated together. Pulling rank on peers weakens your authority each time you do it.

questions.question: 你开始带一位 manager。skip-level 时，他团队的工程师抱怨他定的某个技术方案。你该怎么回应？
options: 把这条投诉记下来，留到 manager 的绩效评估时再体现
当场认同这个方案确实有问题，并答应他会亲自去找 manager 好好谈谈
谢谢他，问他跟 manager 聊过没有，再私下转给 manager 处理
直接给这位工程师一个替代方案，让他先按新方案推进
questions.explanation: skip-level 只用来收集信号，不用来下指示；当场表态会一次打掉 manager 在团队里的威信，绕过他指挥他的人会造成两个老板。正确做法是让 manager 来处理，你只在他需要时帮忙。
questions.question_en: You've started managing a manager. In a skip-level, an engineer on their team complains about a technical approach the manager chose. How should you respond?
options_en: Note the complaint and save it for the manager's performance review
Agree on the spot that the approach is flawed and promise to talk to the manager yourself
Thank them, ask if they've talked to the manager, then pass it to the manager privately
Give the engineer an alternative approach and have them proceed with it
questions.explanation_en: Skip-levels are for gathering signal, not giving direction; siding with the engineer on the spot undercuts the manager's authority, and directing their people around them creates two bosses. Let the manager handle it and help only if asked.
